newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - April 23.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - April 23.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Trading through Tuesday was muted as buyers focused on digesting previous purchases, Random Lengths said in its midweek update. Many lumber prices flattened out, with some exceptions. Southern Pine gained, while narrows of Western S-P-F were vulnerable. Dealers filled holes, turning to secondaries.
Wholesalers sold from inventories or traded back-to-back. Railcar shortages persisted and tightness in truck availability also increased, the lumber reporting agency said.

Western S-P-F producers saw only a trickle of sales, leaving prices for the narrows of Std&Btr and #2&Btr sloppy. Formula tallies of Std&Btr 2x4 could be found at $400; some mills held to quotes of $410 or more. A few producers sought orders for 2x6 and 2x8 with flexible quotes. The wides were tight and prices held. Discounts of up to US$30 on selected items popped up in the Canadian market, Random Lengths said.
Eastern S-P-F trading slowed, but mills stood firm on price.

Eastern distributors and wholesalers marked time, deterred by higher mill quotes and the need to turn recent purchases. In #1&2, prices were up $5 on most widths in Great Lakes markets and were unchanged in Canada and the Northeast.

Southern Pine prices trended higher, though 3- and 4-week order files cooled sales at some mills, particularly on the westside. A few producers stayed on the low end of the range to book out as far as possible. Gains of $5-10 were common.
Inland dimension and stud prices flattened in quiet trade. Minor cracks appeared in the prices of Hem-Fir #2&Btr 2x6 and 2x10; resistance was also evident in the wides of Fir-Larch.

Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir sales quited, leaving dimension prices mostly unchanged. Studs rose $3-5. Buyer resistance to higher prices and longer mill order files contributed to the slower pace. Dealers with needs to cover often found wood in secondaries' hands priced below mill quotes. Hem-Fir #2&Btr 2x6 and 2x8 edged up $1-2, while 2x10 slipped $3.

Southern Pine plywood sheathing and underlayment were discounted by some producers, particularly on the westside. But as order files stretched into May, some mills bounced off their lowest prices on Tuesday afternoon.

Western plywood sheathing and underlayment prices were shaky as shipment times shortened to next week or sooner. Some mills held quotes and sold little, while others approached buyers ready to negotiate lower prices. Industrials and specialties were steady to strong sellers, Random Lengths said.

OSB trading was sporadic and prices were flat to soft. Railcar shortages due to flooding were a problem for one North Central producer, but output was not affected. Sales in the South were slow; the 23/32-inch T&G was tight in parts of the West, the agency said.
